samples.summary: Backend has no global exception filter, so every real server rejection on the newly-converted paths is Nest-shaped and now loses its message
samples.evidence: The backend never registers an ExceptionFilter (grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters` across packages/backend/src returns nothing), so its rejections on exactly the endpoints these commands hit come back as Nest defaults `{message, error: 'Bad Request', statusCode}` — e.g. `packages/backend/src/file/file.controller.ts:35` (`new BadRequestException('No file uploaded')`) and `packages/backend/src/file/file.service.ts:106` (the size/type rejection). Those bodies fail `isErrorEnvelope`, so after this delta `packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:217`, `files/download.ts:57` and the six import sites print `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 400"}}` and drop the only human-readable reason the server gave. Before the delta the body was forwarded verbatim, so the reason survived. Only errors from an endpoint that already emits the `{error:{code}}` envelope keep their text; nothing in the backend does. Fix belongs on the new helper (`packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:128`): fold a framework body's `message` into the envelope's `message` rather than discarding it.

samples.summary: `upstreamErrorJson`'s docstring claims the affected commands' skill files 'already promise' HTTP_ERROR, but the files/notes skills never document it
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:118-121` justifies the new code by saying the commands' skill files already promise `HTTP_ERROR`. That is only true for `packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:84` and `skills/slides-import-pptx.md:72`. `packages/cli/skills/files-upload-download.md` has no Errors section at all (grep for `HTTP_ERROR|^- \`[A-Z_]+\`` over packages/cli/skills matched only those two files), and there is no notes-import skill file (glob packages/cli/skills/*.md). So `files upload`, `files download` and `notes import` now emit a code no consumer-facing doc records. Also `packages/cli/README.md:116-120` still tells agents that anything not a typed error 'reports "ERROR"', which these paths no longer do.

verdict.reason: Every checkable claim holds. The backend registers no exception filter: grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters` across packages/backend/src returns nothing, and main.ts:65-72 installs only a ValidationPipe (plus body parsers/CORS), so `BadRequestException('No file uploaded')` (file.controller.ts:35, api/v1/files.controller.ts:74), `File too large (max N MB)` (file.service.ts:106-108) and `ForbiddenException` (api/v1/files.controller.ts:81) serialize as Nest defaults `{message, error, statusCode}`. The only envelope-shaped backend error is docs-content.controller.ts:43-44 (`TYPE_MISMATCH`), so `isErrorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:76-85) fails for practically every server rejection these commands receive, and formatter.ts:127-132 replaces the whole body with `{code:'HTTP_ERROR', message:'HTTP <status>'}` without ever reading `res.data.message`. The consumer sites are as cited and have no fallback that surfaces the server text: files/upload.ts:216-219 prints the helper output and returns immediately, files/download.ts:57, plus docs/notes/slides import (x3 each). The task doc records that these sites previously printed `res.data ?? {error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}` — i.e. forwarded the framework body verbatim — so the human-readable reason used to survive and no longer does. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described (not not-present), nothing elsewhere restores the message (not already-guarded), and the impact is only establishable by reading backend code the diff does not show, so it is not merely intra-diff logic. The intent recorded in the task doc does not neutralise the reachable diagnostic loss.

finding.summary: The new envelope validation is bypassed by the import/upload paths, which still forward any upstream body verbatim
finding.evidence:
The diff centralises the rule "only forward a body whose `error` is an object with a string `code`" for the six content/export sites. Four other command paths reach stderr with the *same* unvalidated pass-through the change was meant to eliminate:
- `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:164` — `io.stderr(JSON.stringify(res.data ?? { error: { code: 'HTTP_ERROR' } }, null, 2))`
- `packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:194` — same line
- `packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:159` — same line
- `packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:217` — same line
These hit the very same backend content endpoint (`PUT /documents/:id/content`, which `docs/design/cli.md:1029` documents as returning `TYPE_MISMATCH`), so an Express/Nest 404/500 body (`{message, error: "Not Found", statusCode}`) is non-null, skips the `??` fallback, and is printed as if it were the documented envelope — `error.code` reads `undefined`. Worse, `packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:84` and `packages/cli/skills/slides-import-pptx.md:72` explicitly document `HTTP_ERROR` as the code agents branch on when "the server rejected the create or content PUT" — the exact case where the fallback does not fire. Fix belongs at these four sites (route them through `forwardUpstreamError`-equivalent logic, or an `isErrorEnvelope`-gated `io.stderr`).

verdict.reason: The claimed bypassing code is not present. All four cited sites already call the envelope-gated helper: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:165 (also 195, 212), packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:195 (also 238, 255), packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:159 (also 186, 208), and packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:217 all read `io.stderr(upstreamErrorJson(res))` — not the quoted `JSON.stringify(res.data ?? { error: { code: 'HTTP_ERROR' } }, null, 2)`. A repo-wide grep of packages/cli/src for `res\.data \?\?` and `data \?\? \{` returns zero matches, so that pass-through pattern exists nowhere in the CLI source. `upstreamErrorJson` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:123-133) enforces exactly the rule the finding says is bypassed: it forwards verbatim only when `isErrorEnvelope(res.data)` (formatter.ts:76-85, structural check requiring `error` to be an object with a string `code`), otherwise returning `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP <status>'}}`. The specific failure scenario described is therefore impossible: for an Express/Nest `{message, error: "Not Found", statusCode}` body, `error` is a string, `isErrorEnvelope` is false, and the documented HTTP_ERROR envelope the skill files promise is emitted — the fallback fires precisely in the case the finding asserts it does not. The finding appears to describe a pre-change state of these files.
